Docs/Configurations

Configurations

Keep task identity, dynamics, joint targets and camera inputs consistent across collection, training and evaluation.

Four parts of the environment contract

LayerReferenceWhat to preserve
Workspacetask/config/workspace_rig.pyShared table and arm-root placement; table center x = +0.180 m, platform x = −0.870 m, arm y = ±0.220 m.
Simulationtask/config/sim_profiles.pyReference profile: 400 Hz physics, 20 Hz control, solver iterations 24/8 and 1 mm contact offset.
Tasktask/config/collection_targets.py and task moduleCanonical environment ID, reset distribution, robot, episode limit and persistent success conditions.
Policy interfaceutils/dex_tasks.py and camera configurationInstruction, observation fields, joint order, camera profile and image preprocessing.

These values describe the reference profile. Save the resolved configuration for your actual task revision. Changing a physical parameter defines a different experiment and may require new demonstrations and replay validation.

Query settings and respect action order

Research checkout required

The module examples on this page require an asset-complete research checkout, its compatible Python environment, and the relevant simulator or model dependencies. The current public repository ↗ contains a README, license and repository metadata; cloning it does not provide the task modules, robot assets, datasets or checkpoints used below. These examples document the verified research interfaces.

from utils.dex_scene_eval import registered_task_settings

settings = registered_task_settings("SharpaAngledClickMouse-v1")
print(settings["robot_uids"])
print(settings["control_mode"])
print(settings["max_episode_steps"])
Sharpa environmentAbsolute target layout
Single arm · 29 dimensions7 Panda arm joints → 22 Sharpa hand joints
Bimanual · 58 dimensionsLeft arm 7 → right arm 7 → left hand 22 → right hand 22

The controller receives absolute joint-position targets in radians under pd_joint_pos. Relative model coordinates must be converted before the controller call. Observation widths vary across stages and can change when the task state changes; infer them from the selected environment and dataset metadata.

Treat cameras as policy inputs

The native-scene evaluation factory enforces the robodex_fixed base/wrist rig at 256 × 256. It can differ from an environment's ordinary default cameras. Check utils/dex_cameras.py and utils/dex_camera_rigs.py when mapping dataset images to sensors.

Record camera names, order, resolution, resize/crop rule, normalization and temporal history. Diagnostic overview renders and operator VR views do not become additional policy observations. A higher-resolution runtime wrist camera is not interchangeable with the benchmark's fixed policy input.

Save the resolved configuration

For every run, record the source commit and local changes, task ID and fingerprint, robot UID, controller, physics backend, simulation/control rates, horizon, observation schema and camera settings. Add the checkpoint hash, action normalization, language-selection rule and episode seed list.

For native scenes, also save env.unwrapped.eval_background_manifest. It captures the background and fixed environment/camera setup. The reproduction guide explains how to pair these settings with per-episode results.
